transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

My sleep has been all over the place—some nights I’m up planning and working on music, and other nights I can’t sleep at all or I sleep half the day. It's just gotten really erratic lately, and it's making it hard to keep any kind of routine.
When you're up late working on music and feel very energetic, do these periods last for several days and feel noticeably different from your usual self?

Yes, those bursts definitely last for several days at a time and feel completely different from my normal self. I get this restless, amped-up energy where I'm jumping from task to task, and I can easily get by on just three or four hours of sleep while feeling totally fine. It's a massive contrast to how I usually am, especially compared to my low periods.
Have you had periods of low mood, little interest in activities, or feeling down most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yeah, I've been stuck in a really heavy, low mood almost every day for about three months now. I wake up with this sinking feeling in my chest and just lie on the couch, completely losing interest in playing guitar or coding. It feels like I've just crashed and can't get myself moving at all.

Have you ever had a period of abnormally elevated or irritable mood, along with increased energy or activity, that lasted for at least four consecutive days and was severe enough to affect your functioning?

Yes, I've been experiencing those high-energy, irritable phases since my early twenties, and they easily last a week or more at a time. I get incredibly restless, snap at my wife, and take on way too many projects at once, which ultimately hurts our finances and my job prospects when I eventually crash.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F31", "F32"], but based on this conversation, F32 (depressive episode) is now less likely as a standalone diagnosis because the patient reports clear episodes of abnormally elevated/irritable mood with increased energy, lasting at least four days (in fact, over a week), accompanied by decreased need for sleep, hyperactivity, and significant functional impairment. These features meet criteria for a manic episode, which points strongly toward a bipolar disorder diagnosis (F31). The presence of both manic episodes and major depressive episodes further supports F31 as the most appropriate category.
